- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly above recent high.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in next 3–5 days if sentiment cools.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if model consistently forecasts 0.5–1.0% below true price over 3–5 days, adjust upward by 0.3–0.7% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile (±0.33+ in 3+ consecutive days) — add 0.2–0.8% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often misses upward correction — add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to account for sentiment lag.
